qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Turbine certification and installed base service contracts offer modest continuity, but wind turbine manufacturing is a commoditized, capital-intensive business subject to fierce auction bidding, cost inflation, and aggressive Chinese OEM competition. 5-year median ROIC is negative with cumulative net losses exceeding EUR 1.1B between 2020-2023.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Proof of Moat & Pricing Power). Nordex is a commoditized wind turbine manufacturer lacking economic moat or through-cycle pricing power. The company suffered heavy net losses in four of the last five years (cumulative losses exceeding EUR 1.1B between 2020-2023, with barely EUR 8.8M net income in 2024). Multi-cycle ROIC is negative, gross margins are razor-thin, and the business remains vulnerable to aggressive OEM competition and subsidy auction pricing pressure.
qualitative.evidence: Financial performance across the 2020-2024 cycle shows negative returns on capital and persistent operating losses: Net Loss of EUR -129.7M (2020), EUR -230.2M (2021), EUR -497.8M (2022), EUR -302.8M (2023), and a marginal Net Income of EUR 8.8M in 2024. The company does not achieve the 12% ROIC hurdle. Wind turbine manufacturing is characterized by fixed-price project exposure, component cost inflation, and fierce price competition from Western peers (Vestas, GE Vernova) and low-cost Chinese manufacturers.
